effective_rule: registered only by a merge to main of this file with status 'registered' and a launch decision written by the job; PS1 v3 continues unchanged and is not a control that this successor may modify
question: Does a no-trade band on the sizing weight reduce B2's turnover cost enough that B2 sizing beats VOL sizing in after-cost risk-adjusted return under STRESSED costs?
motivation: discovery data, not evidence: PS1 v3 through 2026-10-19T16:22Z (92 closed intervals, 400 h, 2 complete blocks) - ordinary net B2 -0.93%, VOL -1.50%, FIXED -1.07%; stressed B2 -1.56%, VOL -1.55%, FIXED -1.10%; B2 ordinary costs 808.40 vs VOL 66.21 (12.2x), annualized turnover 156.4 vs 13.3
primary: Sharpe(B2, band 0.05, every 1) - Sharpe(VOL, band 0.05, every 1), duration-weighted annualized log-return Sharpe, STRESSED costs (ps1-costs-1 stressed: 10 bp fee + 10 bp slippage + full spread)
secondary: every other candidate pair, reported with the family count (11 secondary comparisons) and never promoted on its own
conventions: identical to PS1 v3: decisions, quote eligibility, fill model, missing-data joint rule, time accounting, capital and marking (desk/research/ps1/protocol.json sha256 d0e8c837...); the band is applied to each arm's PS1 target weight by lab/turnover.apply_band
uncertainty: moving-block bootstrap as PS1 (blocks of 42 intervals, 5,000 resamples, seed 20261019); no interval below 10 complete blocks

checkpoints.C1: 180 days after launch and >= 10 blocks: descriptive
checkpoints.C2: 365 days and >= 20 blocks: status vocabulary of PS1

claims_boundary: sizing and turnover on one synthetic spot policy; no direction, no live fills, no capacity
